name: Koro Zuba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Decker et al. 2021 socioling survey and Sterk 1977 wordlists; no phonological description found.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. Sociolinguistic Profile of the Kami [kmi] Language of Niger State, Nigeria with Additional Observations on Nupe Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-021. Dallas: SIL International. 57 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.2 (pp. 11-12) and 6.6 re-classify Koro Zuba as a Nupe (Nupoid) language on lexical similarity; secs. 6.3-6.5 compare segments across the Koro Zuba, Asu, Dibo, Gupa, Kami, Kakanda wordlists (fricatives, affricates, nasal loss, [ɸ]); Appendix E (p. 39): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' The only occurrences of the string 'tone' are the gloss 'stone'; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Samuel Eju, Adedamola Aregbesola, Fittokka Gobak, Andrew Lewinan, Luther Hon & Thelma Araokanmi. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Koro Nulu [vkn] and Koro Zuba [vkz], formerly Ija-Zuba [vki], Languages of Central Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-051. Dallas: SIL International. 58 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3.2 (pp. 16-17) gives only tentative phonetic consonant/vowel inventories of Koro Zuba from the 348-item wordlist (Zuba and Chachi villages, 2019), noting labialized consonants and [ɸ, β, v, ɗ, z, ʒ, h]; 8.3.3 (p. 21) vowel/consonant correspondences with Dibo; sec. 8.1 (p. 12): 'no one has previously collected linguistic data'; Appendix D (p. 36): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis done of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-032, New Code Request form for Koro Zuba [vkz] (Adedamola Aregbesola, SIL Nigeria; adopted 2021-01-15).
sources.note: Nothing; administrative form (names, locations, population 10-12,000, closest language Dibo [dio] at 30-36% lexical similarity, 7% with Koro Nulu).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014. The Jijili (Koro) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout 12 March 2014). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing on Koro Zuba: p. 5 'there are two more groups of Koro, the Koro-Ija and Koro Zuba... No data was available for these languages, then as now'. The phonology section is on Jijili [uji] only (vowels, consonants); sec. 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading, and the wordlist is explicitly not tone-marked. No stress statement for any variety.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Koro Zuba language' and 'Kami language (Nigeria)' stubs; ISO 639-3 code page for vkz; Wayback CDX listing of unilorin.edu.ng/studproj/arts.
sources.note: Nothing; the Wikipedia stub cites only Ethnologue and the ISO change request. The Ilorin student-essay archive lists filenames by matriculation number only, so no Koro Zuba essay could be identified (the four 2011 Ilorin 'Ija-Koro' essays../koro1323/unilorin2011/ describe Koro Nulu or a Jili-like lect, not Koro Zuba).

sources.citation: SIL Nigeria survey team (Hon, Luther, Eju, Aregbesola et al.). 2019. Koro Zuba 348-item wordlist audio recordings and field transcriptions, Zuba and Chachi villages, Gwagwalada Area Council (underlying data of JLSR 2021-051, Appendix D).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only primary phonetic data on Koro Zuba in existence; any tone or stress analysis would have to start from these recordings. Not published beyond the untoned Appendix D transcription.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2013. The Nupoid languages of West-Central Nigeria: overview and comparative wordlist. Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (cited as Blench 2013 in Decker & Abraham 2022).

sources.note: Comparative Nupoid overview; would show whether any general Nupoid prosodic statement (tone; stress absence) exists that could be extended to Koro Zuba; it predates the 2019 survey and contains no Koro Zuba data. rogerblench.info is dead and no Wayback snapshot was found before the Internet Archive went offline.

sources.citation: Sterk, Jan P. 1977. Elements of Gade Grammar. PhD dissertation, University of Wisconsin-Madison; word lists pp. 252-264 incl. 'Gànágàná spoken near Abaji' (= Koro Zuba per Glottolog).

sources.note: Earliest wordlist Glottolog assigns to Koro Zuba; Sterk marks tone on his lists and his transcription conventions (pp. 1-10) might mention tone/stress for the Niger-Kaduna group. Identification with Koro Zuba is uncertain (Ganagana also names Dibo).
